clue.text: Look for brand on cows and heifers initially

parts.note: to brand cattle is to sear them with a hot iron

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two animal words

explanation.surface: A rancher hunts for the brand on the herd's cows and heifers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C and H, the first letters of 'cows' and 'heifers', and they go after SEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To search is to hunt or seek something out.

clue.text: Not smiling back

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to smile in return.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe and unsmiling; the stern is also the rear part of a ship.

clue.text: Has a high opinion of mid off, when a reserve is out

indicators.note: off suggests these letters are out of their proper order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket captain rates his mid-off fielder while the substitute is off the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, but here 'off' signals the anagram of MID + A + RES. 'when' and 'is out' are padding for the cricket picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to think highly of them.

clue.text: Tunics designed with care but without a number of belts

indicators.note: designed means the letters are worked into a new pattern, as cloth is

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tunics were carefully designed but left without any belts.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of TUNICS and CARE, 'without' the A, rearrange into the answer. 'designed' is the anagram signal and 'without a' names the letter left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cincture is a girdle or sash worn round the waist, so several of them are belts.

clue.text: As term is over for the teacher

indicators.note: over can mean turned over or upset, so the preceding letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: With the end of term, the teacher can relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' signals an anagram of AS and TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a male teacher, often just called sir or master in older British schools.

clue.text: Benefit a small number and suffer for it

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a small number
to ail is to suffer or be unwell

explanation.surface: A few people profit and then pay the price for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or advantage, as in 'to no avail'.

clue.text: Trade unionists bring engineers round reject engine

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union, its members here

indicators.note: round means the engineers' letters go around the reject

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
to bin something is to throw it out or reject it

explanation.surface: Union members get the engineers to throw out a faulty engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps; 'round' wraps their abbreviation around the word for throwing away, with the union abbreviation in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a rotary machine driven by steam, water or gas, a kind of motor.

clue.text: The earliest I could arrange for the facts

indicators.note: could arrange invites us to sort the letters into another order

explanation.surface: Someone offers to set out the facts at the earliest opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could arrange' signals an anagram of EARLIEST + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Realities are things that actually exist or are true, which is what facts are.

clue.text: Full of people getting ready for a drive around Maidenhead

indicators.note: around puts the golfing word's letters round the town's piece

parts.note: in golf, teeing up sets the ball on a peg before driving it
read as maiden's head: the head or first letter of maiden

explanation.surface: A golf course near the town of Maidenhead is crowded with golfers teeing off.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a town in Berkshire, west of London, but split as 'maiden head' it gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: A place teeming with people is crowded or swarming.

clue.text: Just the method for part of the course

parts.note: just means fair or even-handed
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A fair approach to running a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb, but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course, the mown strip between tee and green is where a good shot lands.

clue.text: Doubtful state after being caught during September 1st

indicators.note: after puts the state at the end
during places the catch inside the month's short form

parts.note: SEPT is the short form of September
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
1st is number one, written as the Roman numeral I
CAL is the abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure about a state of affairs after being caught out on the first of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts the cricket catch inside the month; 'after' means the US state comes at the end, and '1st' is the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic doubts claims, so someone sceptical is unconvinced.

clue.text: Accepting everything, until circa the revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: Unquestioning loyalty lasted until around the time of the revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' signals an anagram of UNTIL and CIRCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without critical judgement accepts whatever they are told.

clue.text: Gentleman to go back to one girl

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to go back means the title's letters run in reverse

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman returns to a woman he once knew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns the knight's title round, and it follows the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Question the model

explanation.surface: Interviewing a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question; it is also someone who strikes poses, as a model does.

clue.text: Rustic people are left out of the joke

indicators.note: out of says the side's letter is removed from the joke

parts.note: a pleasantry is a light joke or remark

explanation.surface: Country folk don't get the joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from PLEASANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The peasantry is the class of farm labourers and smallholders in the countryside.

clue.text: Representing the sound or pitch one had developed

indicators.note: developed means the letters have grown into a new form

explanation.surface: A singer's sense of pitch has developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' signals an anagram of PITCH and ONE; 'or' and 'had' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetic spelling or script represents speech sounds directly.

clue.text: Former pupil with big alto arrangement that must be performed

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: an arrangement in music reorders a piece, here the letters

explanation.surface: An ex-pupil makes a big arrangement for alto voice.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is British for a former pupil; then an anagram of BIG and ALTO.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an obbligato part is an essential accompaniment, not to be left out.

clue.text: One's thus managed to raise the flowers

indicators.note: to raise means to lift up, so all three pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: one's means one is, giving I and S
sic is Latin for thus
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A gardener says he managed to grow the flowers in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: IS + SIC + RAN, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are daffodils and related spring bulbs.

clue.text: Endlessly rich coal, replacement of heat

indicators.note: replacement of means the letters are put back in a different order
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Rich coal is being used to replace lost heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts RICH to RIC, and 'replacement of' signals an anagram of RIC and COAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Caloric was the old theory's supposed fluid of warmth, and the word means relating to calories.

clue.text: Refuses to allow a thousand to be deposited inside financial bodies

indicators.note: deposited inside places the thousand within the word for forbids

parts.note: to ban something is to forbid it
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Lenders refuse a deposit of a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: K goes inside BANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending institutions, such as high-street lenders, are financial bodies.

clue.text: Well known for bringing drama on board

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the drama above the board

parts.note: No, also spelt Noh, is classical Japanese drama
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A celebrity brings a play to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing' is a link; in a down clue 'on' stacks the Japanese drama above the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notable is eminent and famous.

clue.text: Stir the porridge

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction for breakfast oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, and porridge is British slang for a stretch in jail, so both mean a lock-up.

clue.text: It's twice cast out some significant figures

indicators.note: out signals letters thrown out of order
twice means the preceding word is used two times over

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone twice throws away important numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: ITS twice plus CAST, rearranged as 'out' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Statistics are numerical data, the figures that carry significance.

clue.text: Alter the position of the dress

explanation.surface: A tailor moves the dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift is to move something; a shift is also a loose straight dress.

clue.text: Tory/Labour split

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, the Tory party
Labour is on the political left

explanation.surface: A rift between Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory and Labour are Britain's main right and left parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft means divided in two, like a cleft chin.

clue.text: It could add muscle to shaky editors

indicators.note: shaky means wobbling, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Something to strengthen nervous editors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaky' signals an anagram of EDITORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic drugs of this type are taken to build muscle mass.

clue.text: Good walker? Better!

parts.note: an ambler is someone who walks slowly

explanation.surface: Is a good hiker even better?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like 'superior', but it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bettor wagers money, as a punter does.

clue.text: Stay back -child is in middle of the vessels

indicators.note: in middle of places the youngster's letters at the centre
back means the word runs in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells a child to stay back from the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: STAY backwards is YATS, with CH in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sailing boats, which are ships or craft.

clue.text: Powerful businessman

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A mighty tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'businessman' splits into business, short for company, and man, short for gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and convincing.
